description: Issue #867 (PR #884 cross-vendor review fix): same patch and same target line as wtmsec867-gateway-type-guard-neutralize (`if (IsBannedGatewayType(memberType)) return false;`, src/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core/Helper/RequestBindingPolicy.cs), verified from the OTHER test project against the five specific bypass shapes the review named -- an alias property, new-shadowing, an interface-typed member, an intermediate base class, and a closed generic type parameter. The version of this policy that first shipped in PR #884 checked member.DeclaringType plus a curated name set; every one of these five shapes changes the resolved member's name or declaring class away from what that check recognised, while leaving the resolved TYPE (Configs, in every fixture) unchanged -- so all five sailed through the original check and only the type-based rewrite catches them. RequestBindingPolicyTests867.IsPathAllowed_AliasProperty_ReturnsFalse / IsPathAllowed_NewShadowedConfigInfo_ReturnsFalse / IsPathAllowed_InterfaceTypedGatewayAlias_ReturnsFalse / IsPathAllowed_AliasOnIntermediateBaseClass_ReturnsFalse / IsPathAllowed_GenericTypeParameterClosedOverConfigs_ReturnsFalse each build exactly one shape and assert IsPathAllowed returns false; with the type guard neutralized all five instead return true (Configs is reachable), which is what turns each assertion red. The green control, IsPathAllowed_SearcherDotCustomFilterField_ReturnsTrue, exercises a legitimate non-gateway-typed Searcher.ZipCode path and is genuinely unaffected by this mutant.
target_symbol: RequestBindingPolicy.IsPathAllowed(Type, string, string) -- the `if (IsBannedGatewayType(memberType)) return false;` guard condition

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.Helper.Request: 'Settings' is declared on AliasVM, not BaseVM, and named nothing the old policy recognised
'ConfigInfo' declared with 'new' on ShadowVM resolves \(as the sole, most-derived member\) to type Configs
'Ctx' is declared on InterfaceTypedVM and resolves to the INTERFACE type IDataContext
'Gateway' is declared on the OPEN generic GenericGatewayBase<TGateway>

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured verbatim against a clean checkout with the mutant patch applied (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first): all five red tests failed at their Assert.IsFalse(...) call with the message text quoted in each red_expected_assertion_patterns entry above (each message contains the fixture-specific explanation of which bypass shape it constructs). Confirmed via python3 test/mutants/run_mutant.py --mutant wtmsec867-gateway-type-guard-neutralize-shapes: 'VERDICT: KILLED' / 'GATE: PASS' (all five listed as failed with expected assertion message in the same run).
